messages:
ana: Heads up — AcmePay reporting a sudden wave of 429s in eu-west-1 since ~09:12 UTC. They say overall qps looks the same but spikes every 2m. Customer says it's impacting payments reconciliation jobs :grimacing:

michael: Can you paste a sample response headers + request-id? need x-rate-limit / Retry-After to see which limiter hit.

ana: (typo) meant ana — attaching minimal log they sent below.

ana: ```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
X-Request-Id: rwd-01f9c3a4
X-RateLimit-Limit-Minute: 600
X-RateLimit-Remaining-Minute: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset-Minute: 12
Retry-After: 7
Content-Type: application/json

{"error":"rate_limit_exceeded","message":"minute quota exhausted"}
```

jess: Ok that shows minute quota exhausted (RPM). Could be a burst that exceeded our minute bucket but not TPM. Two quick asks: 1) capture a few request-ids from different spikes, 2) check whether client is retrying aggressively on 429s.

samir: Also confirm whether traffic is coming from a handful of API keys or many users. If it's one API key doing batch workers, that explains hitting per-key minute limit.

rate-limit-bot: RateLimitAlert detected for acct:acct_acmepay key:rk_live_*** window:minute peak:820 configured_limit:600

michael: Good — bot shows peak 820 > 600. Could be cron fanout or retry storms. Ana, can you ask Acme for the client side pattern? Are they fan-out'ing to many internal workers?

ana: They replied: "we have a reconciliation job that forks 50 workers every 2m to call summarization endpoint" — sounds like a staircase. They expect bursts but assumed our per-minute cushion would cover it.

jess: That's the root then. Our token-bucket enforces per-minute and per-second limits; 50 parallel workers * avg 20 reqs = big short-term burst. Two paths: short-term mitigation (recommended) and long-term config.

jess: Short-term mitigations: 1) advise client to add jittered exponential backoff with a cap, 2) stagger their worker start times (randomize or use a queue), 3) honor Retry-After header and avoid tight retry loops, 4) temporary quota bump / dedicated capacity if they need consistent throughput.

samir: I'll paste a tiny retry snippet they can use (python):
```python
import time, random
for attempt in range(6):
    resp = requests.post(url, json=payload, headers=headers)
    if resp.status_code != 429:
        break
    backoff = min(2 ** attempt + random.random(), 30)
    time.sleep(backoff)
```

michael: For repro on our side: we can run a short load test that mimics 50 workers to the same key and verify 429s spike. Use hey or k6. Example curl loop below to reproduce locally (do not run on prod):
```bash
for i in $(seq 1 200); do curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}s\n" -H "Authorization: Bearer rk_live_XXX" -d '{"input":"x"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate &
done
wait
```

ana: Running small repro on a staging-like key reproduced minute-limit 429s consistently.

jess: Next: we should offer Acme a temporary quota increase (600->900 minute) while they refactor jobs. I'll open a quota-eval ticket. Also suggest they switch long-running bulk jobs to our bulk ingestion route (if available) or use a shared service account with rate-limited queue.

michael: Action items:
- ana: draft customer safety email with immediate client changes (stagger + backoff) and ask for request-ids (ETA 1h)
- jess: create quota-eval ticket and include traffic histogram + bot alert (ETA 30m)
- samir: run controlled repro on canary infra and attach logs (ETA 45m)

ana: Will do. Quick question — can we give them a grace burst window config per-customer?

jess: Not currently configurable per-customer in prod. We have a short-term admin override for quotas (manual bump) and long-term feature request to add a burst allowance toggle. I'll log the feature ask in roadmap.

deploy-bot: Ticket created: QZ-8792 "AcmePay minute quota increase request" assigned to quotas-team.

michael: Customer-facing wording suggestion: "We're seeing concentrated bursts from your reconciliation job that exhaust the per-minute quota. To mitigate immediately, stagger job start times and implement exponential backoff on 429s. We have opened a temporary quota review and will update within 2 business hours." :thumbsup:

ana: Sending now. Will paste customer reply when they confirm change. Thanks all :eyes:

jess: Follow-up: once they implement jitter, ask them to run smaller smoke test and send 5 request-ids from a failing window. We'll verify remaining 429 surface and either approve quota change or advise more radical approach (dedicated capacity).

samir: Note for postmortem — add an example pattern to our support runbook for "batch worker fanout causing minute-limit 429s". Include recommended client code and repro procedure.

ana: Closing loop here. I'll update thread when Acme responds.
